decks.name: LeetCode #312 - Burst Balloons
decks.description: Find the maximum coins you can collect by bursting balloons wisely where bursting balloon i gives coins equal to nums[i-1] * nums[i] * nums[i+1]

cards.question: Burst Balloons: You are given n balloons, indexed from 0 to n-1. Each balloon is painted with a number on it represented by array nums. You are asked to burst all the balloons. If you burst balloon i you will get nums[i-1] * nums[i] * nums[i+1] coins. If i-1 or i+1 goes out of bounds of the array, then treat it as if there is a balloon with a 1 painted on it. Return the maximum coins you can collect by bursting the balloons wisely.

solutions.name: Brute Force (Recursion)
solutions.explanation: Add boundary balloons with value 1 at both ends. Recursively try bursting each balloon and explore all possible orders. For each balloon i, calculate coins as nums[i-1] * nums[i] * nums[i+1], then recursively solve for remaining balloons by removing i from array. Base case when only boundary balloons remain. Explores all n! orderings leading to exponential time.

semanticLines: Define class Solution.
Define method maxCoins that accepts self and list nums, returns integer.
Add boundary balloons: set nums to list containing one, all elements of nums, and one.
Define nested function dfs that accepts nums list.
Check if length of nums equals two (only boundary balloons remain).
If true, return zero as base case.
Initialize maxCoins to zero.
Loop i from one to length of nums minus one exclusive.
Calculate coins as nums at i minus one times nums at i times nums at i plus one.
Add to coins the result of dfs with nums sliced from zero to i concatenated with nums sliced from i plus one to end.
Update maxCoins to maximum of maxCoins and coins.
Return maxCoins.
Call dfs with nums and return result.

solutions.timeDescription: For each of 2^n subsets of balloons, we iterate through n balloons to choose which to burst, resulting in exponential time
solutions.spaceDescription: Recursion stack depth up to n levels, and at each level we create new arrays of varying sizes, total space is exponential
solutions.exampleWalkthrough: Given nums=[3,1,5,8]: Add boundaries [1,3,1,5,8,1]. Try bursting each: burst 3 gives 1*3*1=3 plus dfs([1,1,5,8,1]). Burst 1 gives 1*1*5=5 plus dfs([1,3,5,8,1]). Continue recursively exploring all orderings. Tree of possibilities explodes exponentially.

solutions.name: Dynamic Programming (Top-Down)
solutions.explanation: Key insight: instead of choosing which balloon to burst first, choose which balloon to burst LAST in a range. Add boundary balloons. Use memoization with dp[(l,r)] storing max coins for bursting balloons in range [l,r]. For each range, try each balloon i as the last to burst, calculating coins as nums[l-1] * nums[i] * nums[r+1] plus results from left [l,i-1] and right [i+1,r] subranges. Cache results to avoid recomputation.

semanticLines: Define class Solution.
Define method maxCoins that accepts self and list nums, returns integer.
Add boundary balloons: set nums to list containing one, all elements of nums, and one.
Create empty dictionary dp for memoization.
Define nested function dfs that accepts left l and right r indices.
Check if l is greater than r (invalid range).
If true, return zero as base case.
Check if tuple l comma r is in dp cache.
If true, return cached dp at l comma r.
Initialize dp at l comma r to zero.
Loop i from l to r plus one inclusive.
Calculate coins as nums at l minus one times nums at i times nums at r plus one.
Add to coins the result of dfs with l comma i minus one plus dfs with i plus one comma r.
Update dp at l comma r to maximum of dp at l comma r and coins.
Return dp at l comma r.
Call dfs with one comma length of nums minus two and return result.

solutions.timeDescription: There are O(n^2) possible ranges [l,r], and for each range we try n balloons as the last to burst, giving O(n^3) total
solutions.spaceDescription: Cache stores up to O(n^2) range results, plus O(n) recursion stack depth
solutions.exampleWalkthrough: Given nums=[3,1,5,8] becomes [1,3,1,5,8,1]. Call dfs(1,4). Try i=1 as last: coins=1*3*1=3 + dfs(1,0) + dfs(2,4). Try i=2: coins=1*1*1=1 + dfs(1,1) + dfs(3,4). Continue trying all i in range. Cache each (l,r) result. Subproblems like dfs(1,1), dfs(2,4) computed once and reused.

solutions.name: Dynamic Programming (Bottom-Up)
solutions.explanation: Build 2D DP table iteratively. dp[l][r] stores max coins for range [l,r]. Add boundary balloons to nums. Build table bottom-up by processing ranges in increasing length order. For each range [l,r], try each balloon i as last to burst, computing coins as nums[l-1] * nums[i] * nums[r+1] plus dp[l][i-1] plus dp[i+1][r]. Iterative approach avoiding recursion overhead.

semanticLines: Define class Solution.
Define method maxCoins that accepts self and list nums, returns integer.
Get length of nums as n.
Create new_nums as list containing one, all elements of nums, and one.
Create 2D dp table with dimensions n plus two by n plus two, initialized to zero.
Loop l from n down to one inclusive.
Loop r from l to n plus one inclusive.
Loop i from l to r plus one inclusive.
Calculate coins as new_nums at l minus one times new_nums at i times new_nums at r plus one.
Add to coins the sum of dp at l at i minus one and dp at i plus one at r.
Update dp at l at r to maximum of dp at l at r and coins.
Return dp at one at n.

solutions.timeDescription: Three nested loops: outer two iterate through O(n^2) ranges, inner loop tries n balloons for each range
solutions.spaceDescription: 2D dp table of size (n+2) x (n+2) to store all subproblem results
solutions.exampleWalkthrough: Given nums=[3,1,5,8], n=4, new_nums=[1,3,1,5,8,1]. Create 6x6 dp table. Start l=4,r=4: try i=4, dp[4][4]=1*8*1=8. Then l=3,r=3: dp[3][3]=1*5*1=5. Build up ranges: l=3,r=4, l=2,r=4, etc. Finally compute dp[1][4] using all previously computed smaller ranges. Return dp[1][4].
